LESSON: CAPACITY (HOW MUCH A CONTAINER CAN HOLD)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Measurement
Topic 3.3: Capacity (how much a container can hold)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Capacity (how much a container can hold), part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: how many small ones fill the big ones and 1. How many small containers can fill a big container?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Collect carefully in purposive pairs/groups, observe and talk about containers of different sizes. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect containers. Safety of all learners should be observed especially those learners with chronic health conditions and those using mobility devices.

2. Fill and empty small and large containers using sand or water in purposive pairs/groups.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Collect carefully in purposive pairs/groups, observe and talk about containers of different sizes. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect containers. Safety of all learners should be observed especially those learners with chronic health conditions and those using mobility devices.
2. Fill and empty small and large containers using sand or water in purposive pairs/groups.
3. Compare in purposive pairs/groups big and small containers by telling

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Capacity (how much a container can hold) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size.

Values:
Responsibility: learners work together to carry out filling and emptying activities to determine capacity of different containers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Hygiene: learners observe hygiene as they carefully collect concrete objects and do emptying and filling activities (not to drink

dirty water).

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate water and sand in filling and emptying activities to natural resources in Environmental Activities.
